findings.defect: Two distinct vocalizations are collapsed into one, omitting the separate frightened stammer that follows the monster's cry.
findings.rationale: The source presents the squeal and the subsequent stammer as separate utterances immediately before distinguishing monsters capable of screaming.

findings.current: The Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department thought of only three words: *reinforcements have arrived.*
findings.defect: The source says they thought of the single Korean word meaning “reinforcements”; the draft changes it into a three-word proposition and adds that the reinforcements have already arrived.
findings.rationale: English cannot preserve the source's three-character count naturally, but it should preserve the thought itself without adding “have arrived.”
findings.replacement: The Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department had one word flash through their minds: *reinforcements.*
findings.source: 공안 무력부의 헌터들은 지원군이라는 세 글자를 떠올렸고

findings.current: *Those island bastards are using a method from World War II. Did they not consider that their own allies might die?*
findings.defect: The draft makes the “island bastards” the people currently using the tactic. Shao Shen instead believes the present attacker has adopted a tactic those islanders used during World War II.
findings.rationale: The current subject contradicts Shao Shen's immediate assumption that the attacker is a Hunter sent by China's Central Military Commission.
findings.replacement: *To think he’d resort to a tactic those island bastards used back in World War II. Did he not consider that his own allies might die?*
findings.source: 섬나라 놈들이 세계 2차 대전 때나 쓰던 방법을 가져오다니. 아군이 죽을 것까지는 생각 못 했단 말인가.

findings.current:
Shao Shen forgot there were even humans in front of him and thrust his dagger at a monster that slammed its body into him.

Thwack!
findings.defect: The draft makes the monster's collision a completed action and only has Shao Shen thrust at it. The source has the monster barreling toward him and Shao Shen successfully driving the dagger into it; the blunt “Thwack” also obscures the stabbing impact.
findings.rationale: The next line identifies the monster as dead and collapsing, so the dagger's penetration and the action order are mechanically important.
findings.replacement:
Shao Shen forgot the humans right in front of him and drove his dagger into a monster barreling toward him.

Schunk!

샤오 쉔은 코앞에 인간이 있는 것도 잊은 채 몸을 부딪혀 오는 몬스터를 향해 단검을 내질렀다.

푸푹!

findings.current: Shao Shen buried his dagger in the back of an ogre fleeing with lightning speed, then drew a deep breath.
findings.defect: The modifier is attached to the wrong subject: Shao Shen's skill is lightning-fast, not the fleeing ogre. The draft also reduces 뒤통수, the back of the head, to the back of the body.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly attributes the speed to Shao Shen's technique and specifies the location of the strike.
findings.replacement: With lightning-fast skill, Shao Shen drove his dagger into the back of a fleeing ogre’s head, then drew a deep breath.
findings.source: 번개 같은 솜씨로 도망치는 오우거의 뒤통수에 단검을 박아 넣은 샤오 쉔은 크게 심호흡했다.

findings.defect: “Whew” expresses relief or exhaustion, while 읏차 is an exertion cry akin to “heave-ho.” This weakens the subsequent joke about it being an oddly casual alternative to a death scream.
findings.rationale: Shao Shen expects an anguished final cry but hears the sound of someone casually exerting himself while stopping the airplane.

findings.defect: Taekyung does not repeat or question the full nickname. He mutters “Fuck” and asks what Shao Shen wants, inadvertently confirming his identity through his characteristic profanity.
findings.rationale: The following punchline, *It really is him!*, depends on Shao Shen recognizing Taekyung from the curse rather than Taekyung explicitly repeating the nickname.

findings.current: Korea, the neighboring country that had shared a border with them for so long.
findings.defect: The draft adds a longstanding shared land border, which the source does not state. It only identifies Korea as China's longtime neighboring country.
findings.rationale: This removes an unsupported geographical claim while preserving the source's description of the countries as longstanding neighbors.
findings.source: 오랜 시간 동안 이웃한 옆 나라, 바로 한국이다.

findings.current: *Lord Fuck, whose name echoes across the five oceans and six continents.*
findings.defect: The draft softens the deliberately grandiose image from making the world tremble to merely having a name that echoes.
findings.rationale: The exaggerated physical verb is part of Taekyung's mock-heroic joke about the global reach of his vulgar nickname.
findings.replacement: *Lord Fuck, making the five oceans and six continents tremble.*

findings.current: —The way he controls the undead is a level below this body’s. Wahaha! My legion! This commander has missed you!
findings.defect: “My legion” adds ownership before the Skeleton Warlord has discovered that it can seize control of these undead, blunting the realization that drives the final scene.
findings.rationale: The source addresses the legion without claiming it as his; only afterward do Taekyung and the Skeleton Warlord realize that the weaker control may let him command it.
findings.replacement: —His control over the undead is a notch below mine. Wahaha! Legion! This commander has missed you!
findings.source: - 놈의 언데드 통제는 이 몸에 비해 한 수 아래라는 것. 으하하! 군단이여! 본 사령관은 너희가 그립구나!

summary: Several action, subject, pragmatic, and humor details require correction, including two reversed or misattached actions.
